simple.meaning: קָדַד (qâdad) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to shrivel up , i.e. contract or bend the body (or neck) in deference.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 15 times across Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, 1 Samuel, 1 Kings, and 3 more, beginning at Genesis 24:26. Its contexts include family, family line, sacrifice, Egypt, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קָדַד (H6915).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: קָדַד (qâdad) / H6915 is traced through Genesis 24:26, Genesis 24:48, Genesis 43:28, Exodus 4:31 as a generated source-based concept entry.

structuredEvidence.definition: to shrivel up , i.e. contract or bend the body (or neck) in deference

firstOccurrence.englishText: The man bowed his head, and worshiped Yahweh.

timeline.evidenceText: The man bowed his head, and worshiped Yahweh.
I bowed my head, and worshiped Yahweh, and blessed Yahweh, the God of my master Abraham, who had led me in the right way to take my master’s brother’s daughter for his son.
They said, “Your servant, our father, is well. He is still alive.” They bowed down humbly.
The people believed, and when they heard that Yahweh had visited the children of Israel, and that he had seen their affliction, then they bowed their heads and worshiped.
that you shall say, ‘It is the sacrifice of Yahweh’s Passover, who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, when he struck the Egyptians, and spared our houses.’ ”
Moses hurried and bowed his head toward the earth, and worshiped.
Then Yahweh opened the eyes of Balaam, and he saw Yahweh’s angel standing in the way, with his sword drawn in his hand; and he bowed his head, and fell on his face.
David said to Saul, “Why do you listen to men’s words, saying, ‘Behold, David seeks to harm you?’
He said to her, “What does he look like?”
Bathsheba bowed, and showed respect to the king. The king said, “What would you like?”
Then Bathsheba bowed with her face to the earth, and showed respect to the king, and said, “Let my lord king David live forever!”
Then David said to all the assembly, “Now bless Yahweh your God!”
Jehoshaphat bowed his head with his face to the ground; and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell down before Yahweh, worshiping Yahweh.

Moreover Hezekiah the king and the princes commanded the Levites to sing praises to Yahweh with the words of David, and of Asaph the seer. They sang praises with gladness, and they bowed their heads and worshiped.
Then Ezra blessed Yahweh, the great God.
